key_errors:
src/plugins/intel_cpu/tests/functional/utils/cpu_test_utils.cpp:248: Failure

  Actual: false

primType is unexpected : undef_f32 Expected : acl_f32
root_cause: This is the same recurring, previously documented flaky-test pattern (eb0b94c864ee1a85, now observed 9 times since 2026-09-11) affecting ARM64 ACL-backed CPU functional tests. The assertion in cpu_test_utils.cpp:248 checks that the ACL primitive type selected at runtime (primType) matches the expected 'acl_f32' tag for a given test, but intermittently the executor falls back to an unexpected 'undef_f32' primitive. This is consistent across many different pooling/convert/matmul smoke tests (previously MaxPool, AvgPool, FC, Convert, etc.; now MaxPoolV14), strongly indicating a shared non-deterministic ACL primitive/executor selection path (likely a thread-safety or caching race under the 16-worker parallel test run) rather than a bug in any individual test or PR. The current PR (#39771) only changes tests/memory_tests/tools/run_tests.py (an unrelated memory-test reporting script) and does not touch CPU plugin or ACL primitive-selection code, confirming the failure is unrelated to this PR's changes.
reproduction_steps: Run the ARM64 CPU functional test suite locally on an ARM64 host with the ACL backend enabled: `ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter=*smoke_MaxPoolV14_CPU_4D_2x2Kernel*CompareWithRefs*acl*` repeatedly under the 16-worker parallel runner (run_parallel.py --workers=16); the primType mismatch is intermittent and may require many iterations of the full parallel suite to reproduce.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed CPU functional tests job; this is a known flaky pattern (eb0b94c864ee1a85) unrelated to the current PR's run_tests.py changes.

Investigate ACL executor/primitive selection caching for thread-safety issues under parallel test execution in src/plugins/intel_cpu (ACL executor factory, cpu_test_utils.cpp primType resolution) to determine why primType can resolve to 'undef' instead of the expected backend tag.
Given this pattern has now recurred 9 times across 9+ different smoke tests and PRs, prioritize a permanent fix or quarantine the affected tests on ARM64 ACL until resolved.
prevention_strategies: Add thread-safety assertions or tracing around ACL primitive/executor selection in the CPU plugin's ARM64 path. Track recurrence of signature eb0b94c864ee1a85 and escalate for dedicated engineering investigation now that it has crossed 9 occurrences across nearly two months.
historical_context: This exact signature (primType is unexpected ... undef_f32 Expected ... acl_f32, category Flaky Test) has now recurred 9 times since 2026-09-11 across unrelated PRs (#37783, #37885, #38052, #38528, #38669, #39245, #39251, #39286, and now #39771), each time on a different smoke test (MaxPool, AvgPool, FC, MaxPoolV14, etc.), confirming this is an infrastructure-level ARM64/ACL flake rather than a code regression introduced by any single PR.
